threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Rust document engine with a native CLI, PyO3 Python library/CLI, wasm-bindgen Node/browser APIs, and an optional Python MCP stdio server. It consumes untrusted DOCX ZIP/XML, legacy DOC, Markdown, edit plans, embedded fonts/images and renders or returns edited DOCX/PDF/PNG/text/reports. The Rust library exposes these functions directly; filesystem adapters have materially different authority. Native CLI publication uses staged ambient paths, MCP document I/O uses a held directory capability, Python/Node CLI writers use their host filesystem authority, and browser WASM receives/returns bytes. Explicit self-update and maintainer release/review workflows are separate privileged network surfaces. Evidence: src/lib.rs:7-35,96-165; jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:42-49; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:7-28; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-73,106-110.
assets: Document content, comments, authors, hidden/package metadata, revisions and embedded media; returned text, snapshots, patches and reports can disclose these contents to the invoking application or MCP client. MCP read tools return document text, snapshots, changes, comments and validation data; render returns painted text and font reports in addition to file paths. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,195-218,246-255,279-283,354-368.

Host filesystem integrity and existing outputs. MCP document reads/writes are confined to the directory selected by --root, default startup cwd. Native CLI publication intentionally grants ambient local path access; Python/Node CLI writes also use ambient process permissions. Native publication stages bytes beside each destination, verifies them, and commits individually rather than promising an atomic multi-file transaction. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:69-108,375-381; src/publication.rs:146-225,430-505,535-570; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-132; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-110.

Native renderer font resources and persistent font index, separate from MCP document-output authority. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides the per-user fonts directory; otherwise it is macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Linux ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/jubarte/fonts, or Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/fonts. The default index is its parent's font-index.tsv, not a file inside fonts/. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the index path; empty/off disables it. Index saves use path.with_extension('tsv.<pid>.tmp') before rename. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3090-3107,3182-3229.

Process availability and CPU/memory across Rust, Python native extension and WASM execution. Default DOCX admission permits 64 MiB compressed/per part, 256 MiB aggregate inflated, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison and renderer use the roomier comparison policy of 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB aggregate. Attribute/tag defaults are 1024 attributes, 1024 name bytes, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags. These are input budgets, not CPU/memory isolation. Evidence: src/admission.rs:39-100; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:49-57; src/document_comparer.rs:4926-4927; src/convert/mod.rs:773; SECURITY.md.

Installed CLI executable and software-distribution integrity. The updater targets jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines GitHub releases, checksum asset SHA256SUMS.txt and platform archive binary jubarte. RELEASE_KEYS is currently empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so current updater authority is checksum-only. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82.

Privileged build/release/review authority: release-job GitHub contents-write token, optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, local crates.io/npm/PyPI publishing credentials, and Jules API access. These belong to separate workflows and recipients; their actual grants and runner isolation are external deployment facts. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:230-263,278-308,356-369; scripts/release.sh:919,931-956,1069; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:46-54,259-324.
trustBoundaries: Document producer -> engine parser. Input bytes pass admission before supported package workflows: compressed-size/entry precheck, shared ZIP structural-defect checks, safe/case-insensitive unique part names, encryption/compression restrictions, counting inflation and XML checks. The expected invariant is bounded, coherent package interpretation without extraction or external-reference fetching. The maintainer debug path deliberately uses unchecked ZIP opening to report otherwise refused packages. Evidence: src/admission.rs:439-575; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51.

Raw XML caller -> DOM. Checked try_parse_xdocument/validate_xml APIs enforce input policy, while infallible parse_xdocument deliberately does not; library consumers must select checked APIs for untrusted raw XML. Evidence: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:98-129,910-919; SECURITY.md.

Legacy DOC producer -> distinct compound-file parser. Legacy conversion is supported by read/doc_to_docx/doc_to_markdown and is not a DOCX admission success path. It opens WordDocument and the FIB-selected 0Table/1Table streams and validates their internal structures. DOCX admission independently rejects OLE inputs as LEGACY_DOC. Evidence: src/legacy_doc.rs:172-205,225-235; src/admission.rs:247-264.

Agent/caller edit plan -> document mutation. The engine checks schema version, optionally verifies source_sha256, requires a nonempty author and refuses signed/macro-bearing packages. The source digest is an optional freshness guard, not authentication or proof of human approval. Native CLI adds filesystem identity checks and fresh source hashing before publication. Evidence: src/edit.rs:2073-2105; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1598-1648,1748-1823.

MCP client -> document filesystem capability. Startup resolves --root and opens _native._OutputRoot once; path canonicalization is diagnostic, while actual reads/publication use capability-relative native operations. Output names receive portable-path validation; confined publication rejects output symlinks, defaults to no overwrite, stages all files, uses hard-link no-clobber installation or rename on overwrite and reports partial commits. ToolAnnotations are hints, not separate authorization. Every connected stdio client gets registered read/write tools; there is no demonstrated per-client or per-tool identity/tenant policy. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,152-218,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276; src/publication.rs:146-200,228-273,448-505,535-570.

Native CLI caller -> ambient filesystem publication, distinct from MCP confinement. The caller supplies output paths; held parent directory handles, private Unix staging directories and verified staged bytes protect publication mechanics. --force authorizes replacement but edit routes separately refuse input aliases and recheck original source bytes. Individual commits can succeed before a later artifact fails. Evidence: src/publication.rs:203-225,430-505,535-570; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1607-1648,1748-1823.

Python/Node CLI caller -> ambient host filesystem. Python _write uses Path.write_bytes; Node uses fs.writeFileSync after an exists/force check. Native staged-publication guarantees must not be assumed for these independent writers. Browser WASM's core API returns bytes, and native publication is compiled out for wasm32. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-132; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79,106-110; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:7-28.

Markdown document image reference -> native CLI resource read. The trusted resource root is --resource-path or the Markdown input directory; image names are percent-decoded, URL schemes refused and canonical destinations checked under that root. Reads then use a held OutputRoot capability so a symlink swap cannot redirect outside it. Rust DocxOptions defaults to no caller image loader; custom callbacks carry caller-granted authority. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878,2937-2938; src/markdown/mod.rs:196-198,216-229.

Native renderer -> ambient font discovery/index. Requested font names influence lookup in configured user/system/Word font folders; Word cloud-family paths require a single normal path component. Cached face paths are checked using stored stamps before reading. These operations use std::fs, not the MCP OutputRoot. The font index persists family/path metadata and writes a temporary sibling file. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2225-2235,2241-2315,2637-2652,2855-2862,3090-3107,3154-3169,3182-3229. macOS installed reads include /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental, /Library/Fonts, /Applications/Microsoft Word.app/Contents/Resources/DFonts, /Library/Fonts/Microsoft, /System/Library/Fonts and $HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>. Windows installed reads include ${WINDIR or SystemRoot or C:\Windows}\Fonts and optional %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts.

Explicit updater invocation -> release service -> installed executable. Noninteractive install requires --yes or --check before network lookup; --check does not install; explicit --version permits downgrade. GitHub repository and binary target are fixed by code, checksums are configured, signing depends on compiled constants, and extracted output must pass symlink_metadata().is_file(). Dependency-owned HTTPS, extraction and replacement internals were not inspected in this pass. Evidence: src/update.rs:120-124,144-150,186-257,307-320.

Tag writer/build artifacts -> release-job publication. v* tag pushes trigger version equality checking, platform builds and wheels. A separate GitHub-hosted release job has contents:write, gathers workflow artifacts into dist/, optionally signs them using a step-local secret decoded under $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN, cleans that directory, computes SHA256SUMS.txt and publishes dist/* to the repository release. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-49,51-89,230-263,278-321,356-369.

Operator -> local registry publishing. scripts/release.sh binds a version tag to checked build provenance, requests typed tag confirmation unless YES is enabled, updates main/pushes the tag, then separately publishes crates.io, both npm packages and PyPI. PyPI consumes UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN and dist/pypi/*; npm uses logged-in credentials and optional NPM_OTP; source/tag/artifact checks and registry readbacks are workflow controls, not server-side approval evidence. Evidence: scripts/release.sh:870-901,919,931-956,1044-1069,1095-1097.

Repository PR metadata/code -> privileged automation. Jules PR Review skips forks/Dependabot, uses a pinned external action, sends API credentials and grants PR/check writes while disabling approval. The companion-remediation workflow separately checks same-repository PRs, runs static analysis and comments, then restricts session creation to TRUSTED_USERS=['arthrod'] under selected events; its pinned external action receives a prompt, starting branch, JULES_API_KEY, require_plan_approval=false and AUTO_CREATE_PR. These are distinct grants; external action/service enforcement is absent from this repository. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:46-54,65-92,159-180,259-324.

PR-controlled source -> CI runner. Several pull-request jobs execute on self-hosted runners with repository read token permissions and checkout credential persistence disabled; runner filesystem/network isolation is outside the inspected source. Evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-36; .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-86.
attackerCapabilities: An untrusted document author can supply archive entries, XML, relationships, embedded images/fonts, legacy DOC bytes, Markdown and document metadata to a consuming application. They do not thereby control host environment, process permissions, release credentials or trusted resource roots. Parser failure could affect host availability; filesystem/network impact requires a reachable consumer crossing its specific boundary. Evidence: src/admission.rs:13-27,439-575; src/legacy_doc.rs:180-205; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878.

An MCP client with access to the server's stdio stream can invoke registered read and write tools throughout the configured root and request overwrite=true. That is already granted authority; modification or disclosure within that root is not by itself an authorization bypass. Additional impact requires leaving the granted filesystem capability or compromising another asset. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-218,258-277,300-327,373-381.

A concurrent filesystem writer may alter output names, symlinks or source bytes only where existing host permissions allow it. Native held-directory/capability operations and no-clobber commit address different races from lexical prechecks; do not assume equivalent controls in independent Python/Node writers. Evidence: src/publication.rs:146-165,430-505,558-570; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1648,1748-1823.

A party controlling release assets can replace both a current archive and adjacent checksums; current compiled updater has no signing keys. This prerequisite is release-distribution control, not control available to an ordinary document producer. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82.

A PR author controls branch contents and metadata. Same-repository admission, event gates and trusted-author checks determine which automation capability they can reach. Actual Jules action implementation, provider permissions and repository runner policies are not present in this source and cannot be inferred from descriptive comments. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-54,65-92,259-324.
securityObjectives: Refuse incoherent, unsupported or over-budget DOCX inputs before unbounded package processing; preserve typed refusals across bindings. Maintain independent ZIP structural checks and bounded actual inflation rather than trusting declared sizes. Evidence: src/admission.rs:439-575; src/opc/archive.rs:34-51.

Keep document relationships and Markdown URLs from automatically granting external fetch authority. Native Markdown image reads must stay inside the explicitly selected resource directory; custom library image loaders remain caller responsibility. Evidence: src/admission.rs:13-22; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878; src/markdown/mod.rs:196-198,216-229.

Maintain MCP document I/O confinement using the held OutputRoot, portable output names and atomic no-clobber installation; do not equate tool annotations or canonicalization alone with authorization. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108; src/publication.rs:146-200,228-273,558-570.

Apply edits against the intended bytes when a source guard is supplied and preserve explicit output authority during native publication. Preserve visibility of partial commits and durability uncertainty rather than claiming multi-file rollback. Evidence: src/edit.rs:2073-2089; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1648,1748-1823; src/publication.rs:36-46,83-143.

Treat font discovery/index permissions and environment as native-host resources separate from document-output confinement, including native MCP rendering. Protect the resolved font index and its temporary sibling with appropriate host permissions. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3090-3107,3154-3169,3182-3229.

Keep self-update explicitly requested, checksum-verified, platform-bound and regular-file verified; faithfully describe current checksum-only trust and conditional future signature enforcement. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,120-124,198-257,307-320; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82.

Separate release-signing, GitHub release publishing, local registry credentials and review/remediation API authority; bind release version/source/artifacts and apply each workflow's own event/account/permission gates. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-49,230-263,278-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:870-901,1044-1069; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324.
assumptions: This is an offline generated model from independent architecture review over current source, not completed security-audit coverage. No application execution, network calls, external action fetching, tests, exploit inputs or runtime vulnerability validation were performed. No deployment, tenants, remote HTTP listener or external service grants were supplied. Exact userContext is null; no provided threat model or configured knowledge base.

SECURITY.md is repository policy/context, not independent proof. Its claims about parser safety, resource budgets, external relationships and release behavior were checked at representative source controls; exhaustive call-path coverage remains separate audit work.

Documentation discrepancy: src/lib.rs:9-11 describes byte operations with no temp files, while native font discovery persists font-index.tsv and a temporary sibling through std::fs; src/convert/font.rs:3090-3107,3182-3229. This does not establish an exploitable disclosure or write primitive; impact needs an applicable native rendering path, effective environment/permissions and an attacker-controlled boundary.

Documentation scope discrepancy: MCP module documentation says tools only touch files under root, but actual confinement is owned by adapter document I/O. docx_render and optional edit rendering invoke native engine rendering, whose font scans/index use ambient host access. Retain both the root-confinement claim and ambient-font exception. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:7-9,67-108,185-191,234-255; src/convert/font.rs:2258-2315,2637-2652,3090-3107,3182-3229.

Signing capability is conditional, not a current guarantee: RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None agree with the documented checksum-only phase. The presence, contents and provider configuration of GitHub secrets are unknown. Evidence: src/update.rs:29-48; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-273.

docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 says GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN increases API limits, but inspected src/update.rs:198-210 configures no explicit token. Whether the selected self_update dependency automatically consumes these variables was not established. Do not infer credential recipients or authenticated requests from documentation alone.

Native font configuration is trusted operator input; its absolute values are deployment-dependent. On Unix user_font_dir requires HOME before considering XDG_DATA_HOME, so absent HOME yields no default path even if XDG_DATA_HOME is present. A nonempty JUBARTE_FONT_DIR still works first. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652. Default index paths are macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv, Linux ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/jubarte/font-index.tsv, Windows %APPDATA%\jubarte\font-index.tsv; a JUBARTE_FONT_DIR override relocates the index to its parent; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX empty/off disables it.

Raw XML parse_xdocument and maintainer debug are deliberately weaker admission interfaces; do not import checked high-level API guarantees into them. Evidence: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:98-129; src/opc/archive.rs:15-20.

No engine authentication, encryption or tenant isolation is demonstrated. A hosted application must enforce access/session/tenant separation and process-level CPU/memory limits. MCP's stdio connection and operator-chosen directory are its observed deployment boundary. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; SECURITY.md.

External pinned action implementations and Jules provider authority are absent from the inspected repository. A pinned use statement identifies code provenance but does not establish the service's plan approval, branch ownership, account binding, token scope or publication controls. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:35-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:271-324.

Self-hosted CI jobs exist, but repository/organization fork approvals, runner ephemerality, filesystem credentials and network controls were not supplied. Do not assume an arbitrary outside PR can run without GitHub approval or that the runners are isolated. Evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-36; .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-86.

The long-lived jubarte-rust-inproc executable is a benchmark harness with a stdin COMPARE protocol and ambient input/output paths, not an observed production service. Evidence: jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:5-20,29-68,91-95.

findings.title: Opening a legacy DOC can exhaust memory through reused text pieces
findings.summary: A compact Word 97–2003 DOC can reuse one physical text extent in thousands of contiguous logical pieces. The reader retains one StoryChar per logical character without a decoded-text budget, exhausting host memory during conversion or CLI refusal diagnostics.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can terminate a processing host through memory exhaustion; ingestion is a public library boundary, but shared-service deployment is unknown. Process memory isolation limits impact.
severity.changeConditions: An exposed shared processing service would raise likelihood; strict process limits reduce impact.

confidence.rationale: Source directly connects attacker ccp_text and reusable fc offsets to retained per-character output before DOCX admission.

codeEvidence.explanation: The document supplies ccp_text without a logical text limit.

codeEvidence.label: Independently reusable physical offsets
codeEvidence.explanation: Each contiguous logical piece supplies its own physical fc, which may repeat.

codeEvidence.label: Public reader expands parsed pieces
codeEvidence.explanation: The public byte API passes attacker piece metadata and ccp_text into main_text.

codeEvidence.label: No cumulative logical-character budget
codeEvidence.explanation: Per-piece offset arithmetic resets to fc, allowing the same bounded extent to be read many times.

codeEvidence.label: Retained StoryChar for every logical character
codeEvidence.explanation: Every logical character grows one shared vector until memory exhaustion.

codeEvidence.label: Legacy conversion precedes package admission
codeEvidence.explanation: OLE conversion invokes the reader before DOCX admission.

codeEvidence.label: Rejected input diagnostic fully parses DOC
codeEvidence.explanation: The CLI calls the reader even when already refusing the input, only to generate a conversion hint.

rootCause.summary: Fib::parse trusts logical ccp_text. Piece records independently preserve physical fc, and main_text verifies logical continuity and source bounds without limiting total emitted characters. Resetting offsets for each piece allows repeated consumption of the same small extent while out.push retains every result.

findings.remediation: Charge every emitted legacy character against an explicit decoded-output budget before materialization, propagate limits through all legacy APIs, and use bounded metadata checks for refusal hints.

counterEvidence: CFB chains, arithmetic and physical offsets are bounded; CPs must be contiguous and nondecreasing.
None of these checks bounds logical reuse amplification.
SECURITY.md assigns process CPU/memory isolation to callers.
limitations: No attack input was created or executed; no live deployment inspected.
validation.summary: 4096 contiguous pieces of 65536 compressed characters may all reference one valid 64 KiB extent and cover ccp_text=268435456. The logical coverage and source-offset checks pass while the vector materializes 268 million StoryChar values.

dataflow.summary: FIB ccp_text + PCD CP/fc -> main_text per-CP source read -> retained StoryChar vector

impact.why: Allocation failure can terminate the processing host.

likelihood.why: Requires victim ingestion; actual shared deployment unknown.

reachability.summary: Public legacy_doc::read/doc_to_docx and native CLI conversion/refusal hints invoke the vulnerable reader before DOCX limits.
preconditions: Structurally readable unencrypted OLE/FIB/piece table with valid reused offsets.

attackPath.summary: Provide an unencrypted OLE DOC with contiguous CP ranges referencing the same source bytes and induce native conversion or a command that generates a legacy refusal hint.

remediationTests: Reject repeated-fc pieces above a small configured logical budget while preserving legitimate fast-saved DOC files.
Ensure CLI unsupported-input diagnostics do not fully materialize legacy text.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with a large table span can exhaust host memory
findings.summary: A single attacker-supplied gridSpan value becomes a column-vector length. Normal package admission accepts the small XML attribute, and rendering can request approximately 16 GiB for gridSpan=4294967295 before later allocations.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document ingestion can terminate a native host or trap its WASM instance. Actual shared-service exposure is unknown and caller process limits contain impact; medium severity reflects high availability impact with conditional ingestion.
severity.changeConditions: An exposed shared service or wider victim privileges would raise impact or likelihood; enforced process and filesystem isolation would reduce impact.

confidence.rationale: Offline static source tracing establishes the attacker input, missing control and sensitive operation; no runtime reproduction was performed.

rootCause.summary: cell_span parses w:gridSpan as usize without a maximum; RawCell.colspan carries it into occupancy. table_block sums these values and uses occupancy to allocate/resize cols. row_grid_skip accepts the same unconstrained column count for skipped cells. Physical ZIP/XML limits do not constrain those logical numeric dimensions.

findings.remediation: Apply a supported table-column bound to gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before arithmetic; use checked cumulative sums and a layout allocation budget, returning a typed conversion refusal.

counterEvidence: Package admission bounds ZIP bytes, XML nesting and attributes.
The span remains a short valid attribute and no semantic numeric limit is enforced in layout.

previousFindings.title: Python and npm no-overwrite checks can race output symlink substitution
previousFindings.summary: The Python and npm CLIs separately check output existence and later perform unconditional truncating writes. A local writer in the output directory can insert a symlink during computation and redirect output into another victim-writable file even without --force.

severity.rationale: The local attacker needs concurrent write access to the chosen output directory and a victim with additional file authority. The resulting file corruption is material but constrained; private directories prevent the prerequisite.
severity.changeConditions: Elevated victim privileges and predictable shared output paths increase impact; private output directories remove the required access.

confidence.rationale: Offline static source tracing establishes the attacker input, missing control and sensitive operation; no runtime reproduction was performed.

rootCause.summary: The independent adapters enforce no-overwrite as an exists check rather than an atomic create/installation control. Later unconditional writes reopen the mutable pathname after potentially long work, allowing another directory writer to change the target.

previousFindings.remediation: Use atomic no-clobber installation for no-overwrite operations. Stage complete bytes privately and rename the output directory entry for authorized replacement rather than opening a mutable symlink.

counterEvidence: Files present during the initial check are ordinarily refused.
The race requires a concurrent local directory writer.
Native publication uses hard-link no-clobber commit; MCP uses that path.
No remote document-only exploit is claimed.
limitations: No application code, exploit input or tests executed; no deployed service examined.
validation.summary: The source shows ensureWritable/_ensure_writable followed by rendering and then write/_write, whose default operations truncate existing targets and follow symlinks. No exclusive creation or no-clobber commit binds the successful precheck to the sink. MCP uses native OutputRoot publication and is not affected.

likelihood.why: Concurrent shared-directory race and distinct victim file authority are required.

preconditions: Shared writable output directory and concurrent victim operation.

attackPath.summary: Wait until a victim rendering operation passes its existence check, then insert a symlink at the chosen output name before the final write.

remediationTests: Insert a symlink between precheck and publication and assert no target data changes without --force.
